top_stories.title: OpenAI's $300+ donut-shaped AI speaker arrives 2027
points: Displayless, battery-powered smart speaker roughly the size of a hockey puck, priced $300–$400 with premium metal construction.
Designed by Jony Ive's LoveFrom studio, with moving/animated parts that convey personality during conversations.
Packs microphones, camera, sensors and a listening-indicator light to read its surroundings, plus always-on ChatGPT that can act on voice requests.
Positioned as an AI-first computing device (built to complete tasks, not just play music or set timers) with context memory that learns each user over time.
Targeted for a 2027 release as part of a broader device family OpenAI hopes will eventually displace smartphones.

unique_angles.point: Amazon ran Alexa at a loss for years to gain share; OpenAI enters on a compressed timeline while facing Apple's home hub launch and ongoing trade-secrets litigation.

top_stories.title: AI designs viruses that don't exist in nature
points: Researchers trained an AI on DNA structure patterns from nature, then had it generate genome 'recipes' for entirely novel viruses.
Arc Institute's Evo model produced 700,000 candidate viral genomes, narrowed to 300 built in the lab, of which 16 proved viable.
The 16 AI-designed viruses successfully infected and spread through two strains of E. coli despite the bacteria's resistance mechanisms.
Demonstrates that synthetically designed pathogens created from AI blueprints can be physically built and function.

unique_angles.point: Johns Hopkins experts warn NIH biosafety policies don't cover purely AI-based research, so governance lags well behind the capability.

top_stories.title: Vercel, OpenAI, Cursor and GitHub back an open agent plugin standard
points: Agent Plugins 1.0.0 defines a portable package format for reusable components that extend AI agents (add-ons giving an AI assistant new tools or skills).
Write-once-run-anywhere compatibility targeted across ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor and other agent platforms.
Aim is interoperability so developers stop rebuilding the same extension for each vendor's agent.

unique_angles.point: Some developers argue the spec is so lightweight that client-specific extensions with deeper features will out-compete shared plugins.

top_stories.title: Cloudflare launches Kitesurf, an agent-first browser
points: Browser built specifically for AI agents, running in V8 isolates (lightweight sandboxed JavaScript execution environments) on Cloudflare Workers.
Uses 3–7x less CPU and memory than Chromium by spinning up a temporary instance per task.
Trades pixel-perfect Chromium fidelity for scalability on bursty, AI-driven workloads; free in beta.

top_stories.title: Meta hit with $942M total in New Mexico youth-safety penalties
points: New Mexico court issued a $567M judgment on top of a $375M jury penalty from March over fueling the youth mental health crisis and connecting child predators with minors on Facebook and Instagram.
Mandated safeguards include monthly time limits for teens, reduced notifications, stricter adult-to-minor contact controls, AI chatbot safeguards, and improved review of child sexual abuse reports.
Meta disagrees with the ruling and plans to appeal.

items.title: Tesla and SpaceX confirm $16.8B Terafab chip megafactory
points: First phase of the Texas fab is budgeted at $16.8 billion.
Target is over 1 terawatt of compute produced annually.

items.title: AMD acquires Taalas to etch models into silicon
points: Taalas hardwires model weights (the learned numerical parameters of a neural network) directly into chips instead of loading them from memory.
Its HC1 chip served Meta's Llama 3.1 8B at 16,860 tokens per second, 48x faster than the Nvidia GPU figures announced in February 2026.
Deal expected to close in Q4 2026 pending regulatory approval.

items.title: GitHub Actions outage
points: Webhook triggers and runner job distribution were disrupted across both GitHub-hosted and self-hosted runners.

items.title: DeepSeek undercuts GPT-5.6 Luna on cost
points: DeepSeek reportedly matches ~80% of GPT-5.6 Luna's performance at a fraction of the price.
OpenCode doubled its rate limits ahead of expected industry price increases.

items.title: Shipping side projects entirely from a phone
points: A Spotify ML engineer uses a persistent SSH connection, a mesh network and an iOS terminal client to drive coding agents from mobile.
Stack: home laptop for heavy compute, a connection layer that survives network handoffs, a session manager holding per-project state, and code review via GitHub PRs instead of an IDE.
Dotfiles and setup published for replication, plus a tutorial for running coding agents natively on Android.

items.title: Context.dev turns live web pages into agent-ready data
points: YC startup's API accepts a URL, domain or sitemap and returns clean Markdown, screenshots or JSON.
Removes the need to run your own browsers, proxies and crawlers for agent data collection.

items.title: Meta's Muse Code cuts token spend
points: Specialized prompting reduced token costs on real bug fixes; the technique is now publicly available to reuse.

items.title: SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage crashes into the Moon
points: The stage drifted in an unstable orbit for 18 months before hitting the sunlit western limb near Einstein Crater at 5,400 mph.
Impact carved a roughly 60-foot-wide, 12-foot-deep crater.
European Southern Observatory spectra of the plume showed sodium (from lunar soil) and lithium (from the rocket); South Korea's Danuri orbiter took before-and-after images.
Identification was only possible because one independent astronomer tracked the orbit data on a personal website; NASA calls lunar dumping technically safe but flags rising coordination needs.

items.title: Moderna wins first FDA approval for an mRNA flu vaccine
points: mFlusiva approved for adults 50+ (conventional approval ages 50–64, accelerated approval 65+).
Phase 3 trial of 40,805 adults across 11 countries showed a 26.6% relative improvement in confirmed flu illness versus a standard-dose comparator.
Side effects (injection-site pain, fatigue, headache, muscle ache) were heavier than the standard shot but mostly mild and resolved in 1–2 days.
With 100M+ US flu doses distributed annually, approval clears a path for Moderna's planned COVID-flu combination shot.

items.title: Ford unveils Fathom, a sub-$30K electric pickup
points: Base price $28,350 ($29,945 with delivery), launching fall 2027 on Ford's new Universal EV Platform using a modular 'unicasting' production process.
Five seats, large touchscreen, digital key, bidirectional charging (vehicle and grid can exchange power in both directions), Apple Maps built in plus CarPlay and Android Auto.
Platform is central to making Ford's Model e division profitable by 2029; arrives after startup Slate's sub-$30K truck.

items.title: Hadrian raises $1.37B at an $8B valuation
points: Funding will deploy robot factories for U.S. weapons and aerospace manufacturing.

items.title: ByteDance trains a 10-trillion-parameter model
points: The model is in early pre-training and aimed at rivaling Anthropic's most advanced Mythos system.

10 trillion parameters (the adjustable weights a model learns during training) would be triple Moonshot's Kimi K3, the largest Chinese model to date, and above industry estimates of 8 trillion for Anthropic's Mythos 5.
Pre-training typically runs 3–6 months before fine-tuning and release; final size is not fixed.

items.title: Trump imposes 15% tariff on solar polysilicon
points: The levy targets polysilicon, the refined silicon feedstock used to make solar cells, to shield U.S. supply chains from Chinese competition and boost domestic production.
